stumbles.quote: Colour matches a reference to ΔE76 0.07.
stumbles.why: The post never says what the reference is (a photo? a physical soap film? a spectral model?). ΔE76 is also jargon that many developers won't know, so I can't tell what was matched.

stumbles.quote: Film thickness acts as density in WebGPU compute: thick film sinks toward the tilt, thin rises.
stumbles.why: I can't tell whether the film is simulated as a fluid or only drawn as colours. "Density" is also unexplained. It's unclear whether "the tilt" means the downhill direction.

stumbles.quote: It drains, goes black from the top and pops.
stumbles.why: "It" has no stated referent, and "goes black" isn't explained. Readers who don't know that a thinning soap film turns black just before it bursts may be confused.

stumbles.quote: Not yet tried on a real phone.
stumbles.why: This undercuts the headline instruction to tilt your phone. It leaves open whether tilt input works at all, and whether it ran only on desktop or in an emulator. It also doesn't say whether WebGPU and orientation sensors are available on phones.

point: A WebGPU soap-film simulation in which tilting a phone makes thicker film sink and thinner film rise, then drain, blacken and pop, with colour checked against a reference, though the tilt control hasn't been tried on a real phone.
